pairs.subject: repo-manifest-standard
pairs.evidence: src/lib/standard/manifest.ts:258 Regeneration reconstructs capability entries using only owned fields, discarding foreign metadata and violating the writer-side preservation rule.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/standard/manifest.ts:125 Capabilities use obligation names with command invocations; read.ts also identifies unbacked controls across both placement tiers.
src/lib/standard/doctor.ts:308 Freshness compares commit dates rather than regenerating and comparing owned fields; emitted provenance also lacks generator version and source revision.
src/lib/standard/manifest.ts:258 Readers tolerate extensions, but regeneration retains only command and verified within capability entries, losing unknown fields.
src/lib/standard/doctor.ts:168 The reader substitutes a default location for an absent pointer, contrary to the required distinction between undeclared and declared-but-missing targets.
src/lib/standard/spec.ts:89 The contract explicitly opens extension vocabulary; searches of the context and specification found no reserved or provisional namespace requiring enforcement.
src/lib/standard/doctor.ts:162 Contract versioning and additive evolution are documented, but an unsupported major only warns and processing continues, contrary to this technique's refusal rule.

src/lib/standard/standard.test.ts:490 The specification ships and has an equality guard, but round-trip tests extract the doctor's own subset parser; searches found no independent full-format YAML parser test required by this technique.

pairs.registryProposal: Reconcile the unsupported-major rules: semver-additive-evolution and must-ignore-unknown require refusal, while version-gate-precedes-schema-gate says multi-reader versions are advisory and must not cause refusal; distinguish contract-major compatibility from a minimum reader-version floor.
